title: Switches and Logic Circuits
summary: Types of switches, AND and OR logic circuits built with switches, truth tables, and how logic is used in everyday control systems.

notes.text: Switches can be arranged so that a circuit responds to certain **conditions**. In logic we use **1** for ON (switch closed / output working) and **0** for OFF (switch open / output not working).
When two switches are connected in **series**, the output works only when switch A **AND** switch B are both closed.

items: **Examples**: a washing machine runs only if the door is closed AND the start button is pressed; a guillotine works only when both hands press buttons (for safety); a bank vault opens only if two managers each turn a key.

notes.text: When two switches are connected in **parallel**, the output works when switch A **OR** switch B (or both) is closed.

items: **Examples**: a car's interior light comes on when the driver's door OR the passenger's door is opened; a bus bell rings when any one of several buttons is pressed; a burglar alarm sounds if any window OR door is opened.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: **Series = AND** (all must be on). **Parallel = OR** (any one can be on). Always check the truth table against the circuit.
Staircase lights use **two-way switches** (SPDT), so the light can be switched on at the bottom of the stairs and off at the top, or the other way round.

questions.prompt: Why does a paper guillotine have two buttons that must be pressed at the same time? Which logic does this use?
questions.memo:
✓ So that both of the operator's hands are away from the blade (safety) (1)
✓ AND logic (1)

questions.prompt: Explain in words how an AND circuit works.
questions.memo:
✓ The output is on only when both switch A and switch B are on (1)
✓ If either or both switches are off, the output is off (1)

questions.prompt: A buzzer must sound if the front door OR the back door of a house is opened. Describe how you would connect the switches and say which type of switch you could use.
questions.memo:
✓ Connect the two door switches in parallel (1)
✓ in series with the battery and buzzer (1)
✓ Use reed switches / push-to-break / micro-switches on the doors (1)
